premise.reason: RUN-E5A is LAB-27's release diagnostic re-run with gapX HELD CONSTANT at 0.016, to separate hsS from the guide gap it is collinear with over the full grid (Spearman -0.8177 population-wide, -0.90 over LAB-27's own 16 assemblies). THRESHOLD ARM: the 6.0s run bracketed the transition to hsSRaw (0.0942, 0.1166) - BELOW the bracket that run concentrated in - so this arm samples the 12 candidates inside it plus 2 anchors, at the same per-assembly budget. 14 assemblies, same holdThenRelease protocol, same 6.0s release window, same upMs/releaseDelayMs crossing as LAB-27. Its excess is 1.54% flagged excluding STALLED, measured on an 18,900-trial pilot, and every point of it is TIMEOUT: IMPACTS_EXHAUSTED, ESCAPED and NAN are all ZERO over non-stalled trials. (1) Solver validity is clean by that measurement - 0.0000% IMPACTS_EXHAUSTED, so the axis 2.7 exists to protect is untouched. (2) NOT SUBSTITUTED, and this is the part that matters here. The per-assembly timeout rate in the pilot runs 4.89% to 78.56% and correlates -0.8157 with hsSRaw - the very axis of this run's question, and STEEPER than the -0.5569 LAB-27 declared for the same reason. A timed-out trial cannot be a shot, so the tail suppresses shot rate hardest at the LOW-hsS end, exactly the direction that manufactures a step. This premise therefore covers the corpus's VALIDITY only. It does not and cannot underwrite the shot-rate curve drawn through it. (3) The curve is tested separately, not asserted: a companion run of this identical cfg set at timeoutS=18.0 (three times the release window, LAB-25's own method) is what decides whether these timeouts are observed outcomes or censoring. If per-assembly shot rates are stable across the two windows the step is real; if they move, this run does not resolve the question and says so. Ceiling set at 3% as a bound with headroom over the measured 1.54%, matching LAB-27's, not as a measurement.
